description: 🚀 Team Innovex is a passionate team of technology enthusiasts participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 at Kopargaon. We aim to solve real-world challenges through coding, data analysis, AI, and innovation. Our challenge focuses on harmonizing MODIS and VIIRS satellite hotspot data to support better wildfire monitoring. We welcome creative thinkers, coders, and space enthusiasts to collaborate and build impactful solutions. 🌍🛰️
summary:
FireHorizon is a web-based geospatial platform that harmonizes and compares active-fire observations from NASA's MODIS and VIIRS satellite instruments. Using NASA FIRMS data from March 2025, the platform processes observations from MODIS, Suomi-NPP VIIRS, NOAA-20 VIIRS, and NOAA-21 VIIRS to examine fire activity across India, with a detailed focus on Maharashtra.

The project uses a common 1 km equal-area grid and spatial-temporal matching to identify candidate co-detections between satellite observations. Its interactive dashboard presents fire activity, Fire Radiative Power (FRP), sensor comparisons, regional patterns, and geographic hotspots.

FireHorizon makes multi-sensor satellite data easier to explore and compare. It aims to support researchers and environmental and disaster-management teams with clearer information for fire monitoring and analysis. It is a decision-support prototype, not a fire prediction or early-warning system.
details:
What the project does

FireHorizon is an interactive web application designed to harmonize and compare active-fire observations from NASA MODIS and VIIRS satellite products. It processes four datasets: MODIS, Suomi-NPP VIIRS, NOAA-20 VIIRS, and NOAA-21 VIIRS, covering March 1–31, 2025. The analysis focuses on India and provides a detailed regional view of Maharashtra.

How it works

The processing pipeline cleans and standardizes satellite observations, converts geographic coordinates into a common equal-area projection (EPSG:6933), and assigns observations to a common 1 km grid. A spatial-temporal matching method identifies candidate co-detections within 1 km and 60 minutes. These are potential matches, not confirmed individual fires.

The dashboard includes an overview, fire map, burning calendar, sensor comparison, regional analytics, methodology, and project information.

Benefits and intended impact

The platform makes multi-sensor fire data easier to explore, compare, and interpret. It helps users understand differences in satellite detections, examine fire activity and Fire Radiative Power, and explore geographic patterns. It may support research and informed fire-monitoring decisions. It is a prototype for analysis and decision support, not a validated prediction or early-warning system.

Technologies used

Python, Pandas, NumPy, GeoPandas, Shapely, PyProj, SciPy, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, Supabase PostgreSQL, and Vercel were used in the project.

Creativity and design considerations

The main innovation is bringing observations from different satellite sensors into a shared spatial and temporal comparison workflow. We considered differences in sensor resolution, confidence encoding, geographic projection, data quality, and the limitations of matching observations from separate satellite passes. The dashboard presents these results in an accessible and interactive format.
